In 'Krikštatėviai buvo A ir B, ...' the apposition is nominative, so the entry should read 'našlė / našlys'. Rows 0019_R1 and 0195_L4 already correctly use 'našlė', so do not 'fix' them toward the glossary.

'[B], [husband] žmona' should say explicitly that the husband's given name AND surname go in the genitive, with examples ('Juozapo Bunkaus žmona', 'Antano Drymbos žmona'). Six rows in the sample leave the surname in the nominative.

The maiden-name rule needs a full couple template, because the current one produces 'Jono ir Veronikos, gim. X, Y' in nearly every row. Suggested: 'teisėtų sutuoktinių Jono X-o ir Veronikos, gim. Y' (or 'Jono ir Veronikos (gim. Y) X-ų'). Also state that 'изъ Y-овъ' becomes the nominative singular base (Y), not 'Y-ov'.
Add Каноникъ = kanauninkas with one fixed order, e.g. 'klebonas kunigas kanauninkas [name]'. The sample currently has three orders, and one row drops 'kunigas'.

Say how surname suffixes are adapted: -скій becomes -skis (never -skij/-ski), and decide whether -ичъ becomes -ič or -ičius. The same godfather appears as 'Tyrkšlevičius' (0169_L1) and 'Tyrktlevič' (0175_L4), and Mickevič/Zubovičius/Cynovičius are mixed. Also decide feminine forms (-ская as -skaja vs -ska; -овна kept as written) and require them to decline in the genitive.

Add the identifiable volosts and towns so that Russian adjective endings stop being written as Lithuanian genitives: Ольсядская = Alsėdžių; Ворнянская = Varnių; Тельшевскій/Тельши = Telšių; Дорбянская = Darbėnų [?]; Лабардзская = Labardžių [?]; Андреевская = Andrejavo [?]. 'Текля = Tekelė': the standard Lithuanian calendar and church form is 'Tekla'. Tekelė is a diminutive/folk variant and less suitable for a formal register translation.
Add 'Игнатій/Игнацы = Ignas (gen. Igno), never Ignacas/Ignasas' and 'Стефанъ = Steponas'. The sample has Ignaco/Ignaso and 'Stefano' (0152_L1) next to 'Steponas' (0084_R3).

Extend the clergy rule to given names and to clergy who appear as godparents (the sample has Antoni vs Antanas Józefowicz), and say that 'kunigas' is written out in sentences and 'kun.' is used only in notes.
Add Фольваркъ = palivarkas (0137_R4 already uses 'palivarke' correctly) and сельское общество = seniūnija.

Standardise the editorial markers: the sample mixes [sic], [kaip parašyta], [taip parašyta] and [kaip užrašyta]. Put stray marginal month headings in a fixed bracket form such as '[paraštėje: ...]', and do not use 'juodraštis' for the register entry.

'Bernatovo [?]': '-ovo' is a Russian-style genitive that looks like a Lithuanian genitive. Keep it as a placeholder, but say that it is one, and say that misreadings of Бернатовской (Bunatovo, Beenatovsi) are normalised to it.
overall:
I've read the glossary (docs/LT_GLOSSARY.md) and checked all 128 entries. The fixed baptism formula is applied very consistently. Almost every row has 'N metų [month] [day] dieną Plungės Romos katalikų parapijos bažnyčioje kunigas vikaras ... su visomis Sakramento apeigomis pakrikštijo kūdikį, vardu ...', and the gender agreement between sūnus/duktė, gimęs/gimusi and the child's name is correct throughout.

The main problems are structural and run through the whole sample:
(1) The mother's maiden name is rendered as 'Jono ir Veronikos, gim. X, Y'. This puts the father's surname after 'gim.' as well, which is misleading. It breaks the glossary's '[mother], gim. [maiden]' rule in nearly every two-parent row.
(2) Surnames keep Russian case endings (-ov, -skich, -skij, -ski, and hybrids like -ovas) instead of the nominative singular the glossary prescribes.
(3) The husband's surname in 'X, Y-o žmona' is often left in the nominative (6 rows).
(4) Clergy titles and names drift: three orders of klebonas/kanauninkas/kunigas, Jacevič vs Jacewicz, and Beresnevič/Beresnewicz/Beresniewicz/Beresnevičius.
(5) Russian adjectival volost names (Olsiadskoj, Vornensko, Telševsko) are treated as Lithuanian genitives.

Smaller problems: one date written in words (0187_L4), Ignaco/Ignaso/Antoni given-name forms, stray month headings inside sentences (0007_R2, 0183_L4), the mother wrongly given as plural 'valstiečių' in 0201_L2b, a contradiction between this parish and another one in 0191_L5, a soft-hyphen character in 0018_L1, and 'juodraštis' misused to mean the entry or handwriting.

One glossary entry is itself wrong: 'našle' should be 'našlė'. The rows already use the correct form, so they should not be changed to match the glossary. 'Tekelė' is better as 'Tekla'. Several gaps (canon title, surname-suffix policy, the volost list, the couple/maiden-name template) cause most of the inconsistency above.

I did not flag names transliterated as read where the reading is merely uncertain. Outside the scope of the review, I also noticed baptism dates that come before the birth date in 0062_L4 and 0121_R4; both already carry [?], so they are worth re-checking against the image.
